thesis: A multi-agent system should not treat an agent session, workspace or prompt-visible permission as the final authority boundary; authorization must remain bound to the current actor, execution attempt, artifact, consumer scope and evidence version until the consequential mutation is admitted.
argument: The paper constructs aligned and crossed worlds with identical planner-visible workspace evidence but opposite correct publication actions, formalizing why missing external authority cannot be inferred from an aliased observation.

Its evidence-ablation experiment reports that adding raw authority receipts changes final semantic success from 0/32 to 32/32, while typed packaging shows no observed final-semantic gain over equal raw authority facts.
Its planning experiment remains model-dependent and unreliable even after authority evidence is exposed, separating planner reasoning from enforcement.

Its matched-intent experiment replays the same 32 model intents and reports that an execution-time guard blocks all six unsafe intents while allowing all 12 valid authorized publish intents in the fixed matrix.

Research Center synthesis therefore treats authority as a versioned actor-attempt-artifact-scope relation that must survive to the mutation boundary; Git is sufficient when it authoritatively carries that whole relation, not categorically insufficient.
counterarguments: put all permission rules in the system prompt
treat a current shared workspace as sufficient authority evidence
assume Git is always insufficient for agent governance
equate a lower unsafe-action count with reliable planning
generalize a controlled micro-benchmark into production prevalence
nonClaims: The paper does not establish real-world prevalence of cross-substrate authority failures.
The paper does not provide complete adversarial security against a malicious host or compromised authority database.
The Research Center layered authority model is synthesis, not a paper-authored architecture standard.
The headline quantitative results were not independently reproduced in this run.
